contract: Native client OpenID Connect authorization, app redirect, PKCE callback token exchange, one-time state use and user/session creation. Only selected local-provider and S256 behaviors are asserted.

invariants.contract: The official app's four calls (GET /auth/openid with response_type=code, redirect_uri audiobookshelf://oauth and an S256 code_challenge; the provider's authorization; GET /auth/openid/mobile-redirect; GET /auth/openid/callback with code_verifier) end in a 200 login payload whose access and refresh tokens authenticate, exactly one linked user and one session. The provider URL carries the app's code_challenge and redirect_uri=<origin>/auth/openid/mobile-redirect; omitting code_challenge_method defaults the provider URL to S256; the token request carries the app's verifier. A wrong, empty or repeated verifier follows the upstream web failure branch (302 /login?error=Error in callback&autoLaunch=0), creates no user or session and consumes the flow so a replay answers status 400. A second login for the same subject reuses the user row and adds a session.
exceptions: The native-flow failure branch is asserted from the live v2.37.2 server: a provider invalid_grant reaches the Express error branch and redirects to the login page with error=Error in callback, not the 400 a mobile-only client might expect. The official app treats any non-300 answer or a missing code as a failure and does not parse this redirect.
App-side token persistence and other redirect URI schemes remain out of scope of this invitation.
force is not applicable: no mapped OIDC operation has a force, override or refresh mode.
Client evidence: contracts/clients/official-app.md:108 (native start and code exchange) and :139 (refresh storage). Provider interoperability beyond the local stub remains an open question.
Mapping note: previous internal Go test paths were replaced by the shared scenarios; the historical differential report is provenance, not current proof.
